newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower, July hit by liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower, July hit by liquidation.

text.p: CBOT July rice futures ended sharply lower Wednesday, knocked down as traders exited the contract before first notice day on Monday, traders said.
"Liquidation continues unabated in July," said a trader.
Spillover pressure from weakness in other CBOT grain trading pits also weighed on rice futures, traders said.
Traders noted hedge pressure in new crop contracts, but ongoing uncertainty about world and U.S. rice crops continued to support deferred contracts.
Supplies are tight in U.S. cash markets, but buyers continued to purchase on a hand-to-mouth or as-needed basis.
"You've got a premium (in July) because of the small supply, but that doesn't mean there's any demand either, one trader said.
Farmers own very little old-crop inventory and cash sources report only very thin trade.
Volume was estimated at 800 contracts, which is below Tuesday's actual volume of 715 contracts.
Rice closed four to seventeen cents per cwt lower, with July down 17 at $11.37 per cwt.
